title: Pilotstudy on Process-Based Therapy in Difficult to Treat Depression and Anxiety Disorder
summary: The study addresses the question of how psychotherapy can be better tailored to the needs of the person being treated. Despite intensive scientific research, it is not clear yet how psychotherapy can be improved through greater individualization. This study will address this question by comparing a new method of individualizing psychotherapy (Process-Based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy) with the current gold standard in psychotherapy (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy). The study is aimed at patients who meet the criteria for a depressive disorder or an anxiety disorder. Based on this, the patients have already undergone at least one psychotherapy as well as at least one psychopharmacotherapy. In both procedures, daily self-observations on the cell phone are used. The aim is to determine whether Process-Based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy is superior to routine Cognitive Behavioral Therapy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients will be recruited from the adult outpatient department of the Center for Psychotherapy at Goethe University. Only patients who have previously signaled their interest in participating in the research will be informed about the study.
After a detailed explanation of the study, the patients are willing to participate in outpatient psychotherapy at the Center for Psychotherapy once a week for a period of 24 weeks. They fulfill the criteria of a depressive disorder or an anxiety disorder. On the basis of these criteria, the patients have already undergone at least one guideline-oriented psychotherapy and at least one guideline-oriented psychopharmacotherapy. At the beginning of the study, they are either not receiving any psychopharmaceuticals or their medication has been constant for at least 4 weeks.
Exclusion criteria:
Current psychotherapeutic treatment, substance dependence, posttraumatic stress disorder, bipolar disorder I (lifetime), psychotic disorder (lifetime), borderline type emotionally unstable personality disorder, brain organic disorders, acute suicidality, suicide attempt in the past 6 months, serious medical circumstances precluding psychotherapy, medication changes in the 4 weeks before study participation, or mental disorders requiring treatment in a different setting (eg, BMI<16.5).
